title: Trainyard Mouthpiece
style: Folk-pop with a steady mid-tempo stomp and brushed percussion, built around lead harmonica phrases answering the vocal melody; verse stays sparse with fingerpicked acoustic and upright bass, pre-chorus opens with handclaps and a rising tambourine, chorus blooms with stacked harmonica harmonies and soft gang vocal support. Main voice is close-mic and intimate, with short delay throws on hook words, while backing singers only reinforce key lines in parentheses. Small mouth harp fills, breathy swells, and a final lift of tambourine and acoustic strum add movement. Warm, bright, and human
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I came out a pocket case
all brass and reed
You found my side
and took the lead

Put your hands here
count that breath
One step in
then hold it steady

I was made for
the small sweet sound
When you lean in close
I can turn around

[Pre-Chorus]
Blow like you're calling home
Draw like you're pulling me slow
Easy now
let it show

I’ll catch your shaking hands
I’ll teach your lips to land
One clean note
then another one

[Chorus]
I’m the one that sings
I’m the one that sings
(play me, play me)

You learn me by heart
You learn me by heart
(hold it, hold it)

One breath, one bend
One breath, one bend
(I’m right here)

I’m the one that sings
I’m the one that sings
(play me, play me)

[Verse 2]
You missed the first note
laughed it off
Then found the groove
when the hard breath soft

Little rain on tin
boots on wood
Suddenly your room
felt almost good

I answered back
with a trembling slide
You smiled like
you got it right

I’ll teach your lips to land
One clean note

[Chorus]

I’m the one that sings
(play me, play me)

You learn me by heart
(hold it, hold it)

(I’m right here)

I’m the one that sings
I’m the one that sings
(play me, play me)

I’ll show you how
to make it cry

Just let the air
